claim: In mammalian cortex, excitatory sister neurons assemble into shared microcircuits.
source: In mammalian cortex, excitatory sister neurons assemble into shared microcircuits.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Xu et al., 2014; Yu et al., 2009) as indicated in the Introduction section.

claim: In Drosophila, sister neurons with different levels of Notch expression (NotchON/NotchOFF) develop distinct identities and diverge into separate circuits.
source: In Drosophila, in contrast, sister neurons with different levels of Notch expression (NotchON/NotchOFF) develop distinct identities and diverge into separate circuits.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Artavanis-Tsakonas et al., 1999; Endo et al., 2007; Harris et al., 2015; Lacin et al., 2019; Lacin and Truman, 2016; Mark et al., 2021; Pinto-Teixeira and Desplan, 2014; Skeath and Doe, 1998) as indicated in the Introduction.

claim: It remains unknown whether Notch-differentiated clonally related neurons in vertebrates integrate into shared or distinct circuits.
source: but it remains unknown whether these clonally related neurons integrate into shared circuits.
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: Each p2 progenitor makes a final paired division into an excitatory V2a (NotchOFF) and an inhibitory V2b (NotchON) neuron via asymmetric expression of Delta ligands and subsequent Notch-mediated lateral inhibition.
source: Each p2 progenitor makes a final paired division into an excitatory V2a (NotchOFF) and an inhibitory V2b (NotchON) neuron via asymmetric expression of Delta ligands and subsequent Notch-mediated lateral inhibition (Del Barrio et al., 2007; Francius et al., 2016; Kimura et al., 2008; Okigawa et al., 2014; Peng et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Del Barrio et al., 2007; Francius et al., 2016; Kimura et al., 2008; Okigawa et al., 2014; Peng et al., 2007).

claim: Both V2a and V2b neurons project axons ipsilaterally and caudally.
source: Although both V2a and V2b neurons project axons ipsilaterally and caudally, these neuron classes differ in other aspects.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Introduction.

claim: V2a interneurons express vsx2 (chx10) and provide glutamatergic drive onto motor populations.
source: V2a interneurons express vsx2 (referred to as chx10 in this paper for clarity) and provide glutamatergic drive onto motor populations (Kimura et al., 2006)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Kimura et al., 2006).

claim: V2b interneurons express gata3 and provide glycinergic and GABAergic inhibition onto motor populations.
source: whereas V2b interneurons express gata3 and provide glycinergic and GABAergic inhibition onto motor populations (Andrzejczuk et al., 2018; Callahan et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Andrzejczuk et al., 2018; Callahan et al., 2019).

claim: V2b neurons support flexor/extensor alternation through reciprocal inhibition in limb circuits.
source: V2b neurons also support flexor/extensor alternation through reciprocal inhibition in limb circuits (Britz et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Britz et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2014).

claim: Using a sparse labeling approach, individual pairs of sister V2a/b neurons arising from a single progenitor were directly observed and identified.
source: Using a sparse labeling approach, we directly observed and identified individual pairs of sister V2a/b neurons arising from a single progenitor.
evidence: This is a methodological claim describing the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Sister V2a/b neurons share anatomical characteristics.
source: Our morphological and electrophysiological analyses reveal that although sister V2a/b neurons share anatomical characteristics, these sister neurons diverge into separate circuits, with largely distinct presynaptic and postsynaptic partners.
evidence: This claim is supported by morphological data presented in the Results section.

claim: Sister V2a/b neurons diverge into separate circuits, with largely distinct presynaptic and postsynaptic partners.
source: Our morphological and electrophysiological analyses reveal that although sister V2a/b neurons share anatomical characteristics, these sister neurons diverge into separate circuits, with largely distinct presynaptic and postsynaptic partners.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by electrophysiological data presented in the Results section.

claim: This is the first assessment of circuit integration of Notch-differentiated clonally related neurons in vertebrate models.
source: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first assessment of circuit integration of Notch-differentiated clonally related neurons in vertebrate models.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the study based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: In both zebrafish and mice, vsx1+ progenitors give rise to two distinct daughter populations, V2a and V2b neurons.
source: In both zebrafish and mice, vsx1+ progenitors give rise to two distinct daughter populations, V2a and V2b neurons (Kimura et al., 2008; Peng et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Kimura et al., 2008; Peng et al., 2007).

claim: Individual vsx1+ progenitors undergo a final paired division into one V2a (NotchOFF) and one V2b neuron (NotchON).
source: Using transgenic zebrafish, individual vsx1+ progenitors have been shown to undergo a final paired division into one V2a (NotchOFF) and one V2b neuron (NotchON) (Figure 1A; Kimura et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Kimura et al., 2008) and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Progenitors became elongated before dividing into two distinct cells.
source: Progenitors became elongated before dividing into two distinct cells.
evidence: This is an observation from time-lapse imaging described in the Results section.

claim: In 61/92 (66.3%) of vsx1 GFP+ pairs in chx10:Red background, one identified V2a neuron was included.
source: However, among clonal pairs imaged in the chx10:Red background, only 61/92 (66.3%) of vsx1 GFP+ pairs included one identified V2a neuron (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the imaging experiments, shown in Figure 1E.

claim: In the gata3:Red background, 35/38 (92.1%) of vsx1 GFP+ pairs included one identified V2b neuron.
source: In contrast, in the gata3:Red background, 35/38 (92.1%) of vsx1 GFP+ pairs included one identified V2b neuron (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the imaging experiments, shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Rarely, both vsx1 GFP+ neurons in a pair expressed both Chx10 or Gata3 markers (<10%).
source: Rarely, both vsx1 GFP+ neurons in a pair expressed both Chx10 or Gata3 markers (<10%).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the imaging experiments.

claim: In 25% of vsx1 GFP+ pairs in chx10:Red fish, neither neuron expressed the V2a marker.
source: However, in 25% of vsx1 GFP+ pairs in chx10:Red fish, neither neuron expressed the V2a marker.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the imaging experiments.

claim: There is at least one additional population of neurons to emerge from the V2 domain.
source: Alternatively, there is at least one additional population of neurons to emerge from the V2 domain.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that not all vsx1+ pairs express V2a or V2b markers.

claim: In zebrafish, the V2s population is glycinergic and expresses Sox1a.
source: In zebrafish, the V2s population is glycinergic and expresses Sox1a (Gerber et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Gerber et al., 2019).

claim: V2s neurons resemble V2c neurons in mice in that they both express Sox1a and arise after V2a/b development.
source: V2s neurons resemble V2c neurons in mice in that they both express Sox1a and arise after V2a/b development; however, V2c neurons are GABAergic while V2s neurons are purely glycinergic (Gerber et al., 2019; Panayi et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Gerber et al., 2019; Panayi et al., 2010).

claim: In 16/65 (24.6%) of vsx1 mCherry+ pairs, one of the two sister neurons co-labeled with sox1a.
source: In 16/65 (24.6%) of vsx1 mCherry+ pairs, one of the two sister neurons co-labeled with sox1a (Figure 1D, right)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the imaging experiments, shown in Figure 1D.

claim: In 49/65 (75.4%) of vsx1 mCherry+ pairs, neither neuron co-labeled with sox1a.
source: and in 49/65 (75.4%) of vsx1 mCherry+ pairs, neither neuron co-labeled with sox1a (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the imaging experiments, shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Not all vsx1+ progenitors differentiate into V2a/b pairs.
source: These results suggest that not all vsx1+ progenitors differentiate into V2a/b pairs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the co-labeling data showing that some vsx1+ pairs do not include V2a neurons.

claim: Approximately 75% of vsx1 progenitors divide into V2a/b pairs while the remainder divide into V2b/s pairs.
source: Instead, approximately 75% of vsx1 progenitors divide into V2a/b pairs while the remainder divide into V2b/s pairs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the quantitative co-labeling data.

claim: No vsx1+ triplets or singlets were observed in co-label experiments (0/195).
source: We did not see any vsx1+ triplets or singlets in co-label experiments (0/195)
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the imaging experiments.

claim: vsx1 progenitors only undergo a single, terminal division.
source: suggesting that vsx1 progenitors only undergo a single, terminal division.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that no triplets or singlets were observed.

claim: The stochastic labeling approach successfully labeled clonally related V2 neurons.
source: Based on these results, we conclude that our stochastic labeling approach successfully labeled clonally related V2 neurons
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the imaging data presented.

claim: A chx10 co-label is required to properly identify vsx1 pairs as V2a/b neurons in vivo.
source: but required a chx10 co-label to properly identify vsx1 pairs as V2a/b neurons in vivo.
evidence: This is a methodological conclusion based on the co-labeling experiments.

claim: Immediately after progenitor division around 1 dpf, sister V2a/b neurons are located in close proximity to each other.
source: Immediately after progenitor division around 1 dpf, sister V2a/b neurons are located in close proximity to each other (Kimura et al., 2008)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Kimura et al., 2008).

claim: Sister V2 neurons were usually closer neighbors than non-sister V2 neurons.
source: Across animals, sister V2 neurons were usually closer neighbors than non-sister V2 neurons, whether measured in the V2a or V2b reporter lines (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from distance measurements, shown in Figure 2B.

claim: At 24 hpf, sister neuron centers were ~7 µm apart.
source: At 24 hpf, sister neuron centers were ~7 µm apart, or effectively adjacent.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from time-lapse imaging experiments.

claim: By 48 hpf, the inter-soma distance increased slightly to ~9 µm.
source: By 48 hpf, this inter-soma distance increased slightly to ~9 µm (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from time-lapse imaging experiments, shown in Figure 2C.

claim: V2a/b somata are ~10 µm in size.
source: Because V2a/b somata are ~10 µm in size (Callahan et al., 2019; Kimura et al., 2006; Menelaou et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Callahan et al., 2019; Kimura et al., 2006; Menelaou et al., 2014).

claim: Sister V2 neurons usually remain adjacent.
source: our data suggest that sister V2 neurons usually remain adjacent.
evidence: This is an inference based on the inter-soma distance measurements relative to soma size.

claim: V2b neurons were typically positioned more dorsally than their sister V2a counterparts.
source: Lastly, restricting our analysis to sister V2a/b neurons using chx10:Red fish, we found that V2b neurons were typically positioned more dorsally than their sister V2a counterparts (Figure 2D)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from position measurements, shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Inhibitory populations are located more dorsally than excitatory neurons in spinal cord.
source: consistent with previous work showing inhibitory populations are located more dorsally than excitatory neurons in spinal cord (Kimura et al., 2006; McLean et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Kimura et al., 2006; McLean et al., 2007).

claim: Sister V2a/b neurons develop and remain close to each other during larval stages.
source: Altogether, our data demonstrate that sister V2a/b neurons develop and remain close to each other during larval stages.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the distance measurements over time.

claim: Sparsely labeled vsx1 GFP+ neurons located close to each other at 3–4 dpf represented sister pairs.
source: As a result, in subsequent experiments we inferred that sparsely labeled vsx1 GFP+ neurons located close to each other at 3–4 dpf represented sister pairs.
evidence: This is a methodological inference based on the proximity data.

claim: Sister V2a neurons exhibited axons that were on average 61% longer than their V2b counterparts.
source: Sister V2a neurons exhibited axons that were on average 61% longer than their V2b counterparts (Figure 3B)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from axon length measurements, shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Notch expression attenuates axon growth.
source: consistent with work showing that Notch expression attenuates axon growth (Mark et al., 2021; Mizoguchi et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Mark et al., 2021; Mizoguchi et al., 2020).

claim: There was no relationship between the length of the axons and their location along the rostral-caudal axis of the fish.
source: There was no relationship between the length of the axons and their location along the rostral-caudal axis of the fish (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from correlation analysis, shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Clonally related V2a/b neurons send axons along a similar trajectory, with a median of 37.1% of the V2b axon length within 5 µm of the V2a axon.
source: Indeed, clonally related V2a/b neurons send axons along a similar trajectory, with a median of 37.1% of the V2b axon length within 5 µm of the V2a axon (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from axon proximity measurements, shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The similar axon trajectories suggest a possibility for sister V2a/b neurons to contact shared synaptic targets.
source: Because the axons follow similar paths, these results suggest a possibility for sister V2a/b neurons to contact shared synaptic targets.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the axon proximity data.

claim: Sister neurons in hippocampus are more likely to receive synaptic input from shared presynaptic partners than non-sister neurons.
source: Work in hippocampus has shown that sister neurons are more likely to receive synaptic input from shared presynaptic partners than non-sister neurons (Xu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Xu et al., 2014).

claim: NotchON and NotchOFF sister neurons in Drosophila integrate into separate hemilineages that segregate spatially.
source: In contrast, NotchON and NotchOFF sister neurons in Drosophila integrate into separate hemilineages that segregate spatially, although whether they receive shared input is not known (Harris et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Harris et al., 2015).

claim: The timing of EPSCs arriving in each neuron of the sister pair was asynchronous.
source: The timing of EPSCs arriving in each neuron of the pair was asynchronous, as exemplified by an overlay of several hundred EPSCs from either a V2a/b and the associated EPSC-triggered average in its sister neuron (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This is a result from paired electrophysiology recordings, shown in Figures 4D and E.

claim: Across recordings from 13 clonally related pairs in vivo, there was consistently little to no synchronous synaptic input.
source: Across recordings from 13 clonally related pairs in vivo, we consistently saw little to no synchronous synaptic input (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from paired electrophysiology recordings, shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The asynchronous timing of inputs suggests that they cannot be arriving from a shared presynaptic source, but rather, different presynaptic sources which fire at different times.
source: The asynchronous timing of these inputs suggests that they cannot be arriving from a shared presynaptic source, but rather, different presynaptic sources which fire at different times (Bagnall and McLean, 2014).
evidence: This is an inference based on the asynchronous EPSC timing, with citation to prior work (Bagnall and McLean, 2014).

claim: Sister V2a/b neurons, and any V2a-V2b pair from the same segment, receive input from distinct presynaptic sources during light-evoked locomotion at slow to medium locomotor speeds.
source: Altogether, these data show that not only sister V2a/b neurons, but any V2a-V2b pair, clonal or non-clonal, from the same segment receives input from distinct presynaptic sources during light-evoked locomotion at slow to medium locomotor speeds.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the electrophysiology data.

claim: The possibility remains that sister neurons receive shared inputs from circuits for fast locomotion or specialized behaviors.
source: We cannot rule out the possibility that sister neurons receive shared inputs from circuits for fast locomotion or specialized behaviors.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about limitations of the study.

claim: Clonal pair analysis in cortex has shown that sister neurons preferentially form synapses onto each other.
source: Clonal pair analysis in cortex has shown that sister neurons preferentially form synapses onto each other (Yu et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Yu et al., 2009; Zhang et al., 2017).

claim: Sister V2a/b neurons do not form synaptic connections with each other.
source: In both cases, there were no detectable evoked currents, showing that sister V2a/b neurons do not connect with each other (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a result from paired electrophysiology recordings, shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Non-clonally related V2a/b neurons exhibited no interconnectivity.
source: Similarly, non-clonally related V2a/b neurons exhibited no interconnectivity (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a result from paired electrophysiology recordings, shown in Figure 5D.

claim: V2a/b neurons in the same segment do not form direct synapses with each other.
source: Therefore, V2a/b neurons in the same segment do not form direct synapses with each other.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the paired recording data.

claim: Any connectivity among V2a and V2b neurons likely occurs between neurons in different segments.
source: Any connectivity among V2a and V2b neurons likely occurs between neurons in different segments (Sengupta and Bagnall, 2022).
evidence: This is an inference with citation to prior work (Sengupta and Bagnall, 2022).

claim: Clonally related inhibitory interneurons in cortex form synaptic connections with shared downstream targets.
source: Research in cortex has shown that clonally related inhibitory interneurons form synaptic connections with shared downstream targets (Zhang et al., 2017), although this claim is disputed (Mayer et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Zhang et al., 2017), with a note that it is disputed (Mayer et al., 2016).

claim: All CoChR2-tdTomato+ vsx1 neurons fired action potentials in response to optical stimulation (n = 13 neurons from 12 fish).
source: All CoChR2-tdTomato+ vsx1 neurons fired action potentials in response to optical stimulation (Figure 6C, n = 13 neurons from 12 fish).
evidence: This is a result from cell-attached recordings with optogenetic stimulation, shown in Figure 6C.

claim: All CoChR2-tdTomato(-) neurons remained inactive during the light stimulus (n = 22 neurons from 18 fish).
source: All CoChR2-tdTomato(-) neurons remained inactive during the light stimulus (Figure 6C, n = 22 neurons from 18 fish).
evidence: This is a result from cell-attached recordings with optogenetic stimulation, shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Most light-evoked spikes were observed throughout the duration of the stimulus, with some spiking following the stimulus window.
source: In CoChR2-tdTomato+ neurons, most light-evoked spikes were observed throughout the duration of the stimulus, with some spiking following the stimulus window (Figure 6C and E).
evidence: This is a result from cell-attached recordings with optogenetic stimulation, shown in Figures 6C and E.

claim: The prolonged activity is most likely due to the long inactivation kinetics of the CoChR2 variant.
source: This prolonged activity is most likely due to the long inactivation kinetics of the CoChR2 variant (Antinucci et al., 2020).
evidence: This is an inference based on known properties of CoChR2, with citation to prior work (Antinucci et al., 2020).

claim: The optogenetic approach is a feasible method for assessing downstream connectivity of sister V2a/b neurons.
source: Altogether, our optogenetic approach is a feasible method for assessing downstream connectivity of sister V2a/b neurons.
evidence: This is a methodological conclusion based on the validation experiments.

claim: In most recorded neurons, optical stimuli evoked neither EPSCs nor IPSCs (n = 85/99).
source: In most recorded neurons, optical stimuli evoked neither EPSCs nor IPSCs, consistent with sparse connectivity in the spinal cord (n = 85/99; Figure 7E and F).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from optogenetic stimulation experiments, shown in Figures 7E and F.

claim: In six target neurons, evoked EPSCs but not IPSCs were recorded, demonstrating that the target neuron received synaptic input from the CoChR2-labeled V2a neuron but not the V2b.
source: In six target neurons, we recorded evoked EPSCs (Vhold –80 mV) but not IPSCs, demonstrating that the target neuron received synaptic input from the CoChR2-labeled V2a neuron but not the V2b (Figure 7B and E).
evidence: This is a result from optogenetic stimulation experiments, shown in Figures 7B and E.

claim: In six target neurons, evoked IPSCs but no EPSCs were detected, demonstrating that the target neuron received synaptic input from the V2b but not the V2a neuron.
source: In another six target neurons, we detected evoked IPSCs (Vhold 0 mV) but no EPSCs, demonstrating that the target neuron received synaptic input from the V2b but not the V2a neuron (Figure 7C and E).
evidence: This is a result from optogenetic stimulation experiments, shown in Figures 7C and E.

claim: In two instances, a target neuron received both evoked EPSCs and IPSCs, with the magnitude of IPSCs approximately fivefold larger than the magnitude of the EPSCs.
source: In two instances, a target neuron received both evoked EPSCs and IPSCs, with the magnitude of IPSCs approximately fivefold larger than the magnitude of the EPSCs, suggesting an asymmetric connection from sister V2a/b neurons (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a result from optogenetic stimulation experiments, shown in Figure 7E.

claim: In 10 neurons, a slow depolarizing current was detected when target neurons were held at –80 mV, but not at 0 mV.
source: In 10 neurons, we detected a slow depolarizing current when target neurons were held at –80 mV (Figure 7D and F, gray), but not at 0 mV.
evidence: This is a result from optogenetic stimulation experiments, shown in Figures 7D and F.

claim: The slow evoked current had a lower amplitude and longer rise time than fast evoked EPSCs.
source: This evoked current had a lower amplitude and longer rise time than fast evoked EPSCs (Figure 7G).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from analysis of evoked currents, shown in Figure 7G.

claim: The slow excitatory current may be caused by a weak disynaptic electrical connection.
source: This slow excitatory current may be caused by a weak disynaptic electrical connection (Menelaou and McLean, 2019), but we were not able to eliminate it with gap junction blockers (carbenoxylone and 18-β-glycyrrhetinic acid).
evidence: This is a speculative inference with citation to prior work (Menelaou and McLean, 2019), noting that gap junction blockers did not eliminate the current.

claim: Target neurons were evenly divided between motor neurons (early and late born), and excitatory and inhibitory interneurons.
source: Target neurons were evenly divided between motor neurons (early and late born), and excitatory and inhibitory interneurons.
evidence: This is a summary of the target neuron identities from Table 1.

claim: Clonally related V2a/b neurons do not preferentially form synaptic connections with shared targets.
source: Overall, these results demonstrate that clonally related V2a/b neurons do not preferentially form synaptic connections with shared targets.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the optogenetic stimulation data.

claim: Clonally related V2a/b neurons exhibit similar morphological characteristics, but form synapses with and receive information from largely distinct neuronal partners.
source: In this study, we showed that clonally related V2a/b neurons exhibit similar morphological characteristics, but form synapses with and receive information from largely distinct neuronal partners.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claim: Sister neuron somata remain in close proximity to each other and send their axons along similar trajectories.
source: Within V2a/b pairs, we saw that sister neuron somata remain in close proximity to each other and send their axons along similar trajectories.
evidence: This is a summary of the morphological findings.

claim: Clonally related V2a/b neurons do not communicate with each other, do not receive input from similar sources, and infrequently connect to the same downstream target.
source: Clonally related V2a/b neurons do not communicate with each other, do not receive input from similar sources, and infrequently connect to the same downstream target.
evidence: This is a summary of the electrophysiological findings.

claim: This connectivity pattern resembles circuitry seen in Drosophila Notch-differentiated hemilineages.
source: This connectivity pattern resembles circuitry seen in Drosophila Notch-differentiated hemilineages (Figure 7I).
evidence: This is a comparative inference based on the findings, illustrated in Figure 7I.

claim: These results represent the first evidence of Notch-differentiated circuit integration in a vertebrate system.
source: Our results represent the first evidence of Notch-differentiated circuit integration in a vertebrate system
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: The findings may reflect a means of cell-type and circuit diversification in earlier evolved neural structures.
source: and may reflect a means of cell-type and circuit diversification in earlier evolved neural structures.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: Notch is an important regulator in V2a/b differentiation.
source: Notch is an important regulator in V2a/b differentiation, and during vsx1+ progenitor division, differences in Notch expression result in the onset of V2a (NotchOFF) or V2b (NotchON) programming (Batista et al., 2008; Debrulle et al., 2020; Kimura et al., 2008; Mizoguchi et al., 2020; Okigawa et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Batista et al., 2008; Debrulle et al., 2020; Kimura et al., 2008; Mizoguchi et al., 2020; Okigawa et al., 2014).

claim: It remains unknown whether Notch plays a role in sister V2a/b development beyond initiating cellular identity or whether it functions as an intermediary step before other molecular factors determine cellular morphology postmitotically.
source: However, it remains unknown whether Notch plays a role in sister V2a/b development beyond initiating cellular identity or whether it functions as an intermediary step before other molecular factors determine cellular morphology postmitotically (Kozak et al., 2020; Mizoguchi et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a statement about a gap in knowledge, with citations to prior work (Kozak et al., 2020; Mizoguchi et al., 2020).

claim: Constitutive manipulation of Notch levels results in a skewing of V2a/b numbers.
source: Constitutive manipulation of Notch levels results in a skewing of V2a/b numbers (Mizoguchi et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Mizoguchi et al., 2020).

claim: The recently discovered V2s population relies on Notch signaling for its development with Notch KO mutants showing a decrease in sox1a+ neurons.
source: Similarly, the recently discovered V2s population relies on Notch signaling for its development with Notch KO mutants showing a decrease in sox1a+ neurons (Gerber et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Gerber et al., 2019).

claim: Some vsx1+ progenitors give rise to V2b/s sister pairs in addition to the previously described V2a/b pairs.
source: We speculate that some vsx1+ progenitors give rise to V2b/s sister pairs in addition to the previously described V2a/b pairs.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the co-labeling data.

claim: V2s neurons arise later than the initial wave of V2a/b pairs.
source: V2s neurons arise later than the initial wave of V2a/b pairs (Gerber et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Gerber et al., 2019).

claim: Notch exhibits different effects on cellular identity during early and late development.
source: Because Notch has been shown to exhibit different effects on cellular identity during early and late development, we suggest that delayed Notch activity causes some later born vsx1+ sister neurons to adopt a V2b/s identity, which are both NotchON (Jacobs et al., 2022).
evidence: This is a speculative inference with citation to prior work (Jacobs et al., 2022).

claim: Only early cerebellar progenitors appear to undergo Notch differentiation into distinct cell types, the Purkinje and granule cells.
source: Similarly, only early cerebellar progenitors appear to undergo Notch differentiation into distinct cell types, the Purkinje and granule cells (Zhang et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Zhang et al., 2021).

claim: Lineage pathfinding and innervation differences in Drosophila are well documented.
source: Lineage pathfinding and innervation differences in Drosophila are well documented, and Notch-differentiated sister neurons in these organisms develop different axon trajectories, presumably connecting to different downstream targets (Harris et al., 2015; Truman et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Harris et al., 2015; Truman et al., 2010).

claim: Notch mediates cerebellar progenitor differentiation into excitatory and inhibitory cerebellar cell types.
source: Analysis of Notch-differentiated lineages in vertebrate cerebellum have shown that Notch mediates cerebellar progenitor differentiation into excitatory and inhibitory cerebellar cell types (Zhang et al., 2021)
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Zhang et al., 2021).

claim: It is not yet known whether Notch-differentiated cerebellar neurons integrate into shared or distinct circuits.
source: but it is not yet known whether the resulting neurons integrate into shared or distinct circuits.
evidence: This is a statement about a gap in knowledge.

claim: The results are consistent with a framework in which the progeny of Notch-differentiated divisions preferentially integrate into distinct networks in both invertebrates and vertebrates.
source: Our results are consistent with a framework in which the progeny of Notch-differentiated divisions preferentially integrate into distinct networks in both invertebrates and vertebrates.
evidence: This is an interpretive inference based on the findings.

claim: The divergent cellular identities of sister V2a/b neurons appear to determine that they participate in distinct circuits.
source: In contrast with cortical lineages, the divergent cellular identities of sister V2a/b neurons appear to determine that they participate in distinct circuits.
evidence: This is an interpretive inference based on the findings.

claim: Earlier evolved neural structures rely on Notch-differentiated divisions as a means to diversify neuronal populations during development.
source: We speculate that earlier evolved neural structures rely on Notch-differentiated divisions as a means to diversify neuronal populations during development.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: The presence of Notch-differentiated sister neurons in both cerebellum and spinal cord could represent an efficient mechanism to generate diverse cell types early in development.
source: The presence of Notch-differentiated sister neurons in both cerebellum and spinal cord could represent an efficient mechanism to generate diverse cell types early in development, in contrast to cortical reliance on dedicated streams of excitatory and inhibitory neural progenitors (Goulding, 2009; Leto et al., 2016; Ma et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with citations to prior work (Goulding, 2009; Leto et al., 2016; Ma et al., 2018).

claim: Developmental timing allows for proper integration of neurons into functional speed-dependent locomotor circuits.
source: Developmental timing allows for proper integration of neurons into functional speed-dependent locomotor circuits.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Discussion.

claim: In zebrafish, motor neurons and interneurons born during similar developmental windows are active and recruited at similar speeds.
source: In zebrafish, motor neurons and interneurons born during similar developmental windows are active and recruited at similar speeds (McLean et al., 2007; McLean and Fetcho, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (McLean et al., 2007; McLean and Fetcho, 2009).

claim: Birthdate-dependent microcircuits emerge in larvae and persist into adulthood.
source: These birthdate-dependent microcircuits emerge in larvae and persist into adulthood (Ampatzis et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Ampatzis et al., 2014).

claim: vsx1+ sister neurons share a birthdate.
source: By definition, vsx1+ sister neurons share a birthdate
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the definition of sister neurons.

claim: Sister V2a/b divergence in cellular identity may cause integration into different hemilineage temporal cohorts, similar to Drosophila, which then determine their neuronal connectivity.
source: One possible explanation is that sister V2a/b divergence in cellular identity may cause integration into different hemilineage temporal cohorts, similar to Drosophila, which then determine their neuronal connectivity (Mark et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with citation to prior work (Mark et al., 2021).

claim: V2b neurons may participate in different behaviors than V2a neurons.
source: Additionally, V2b neurons, whose recruitment patterns have not yet been described, may participate in different behaviors than V2a neurons.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the lack of information about V2b recruitment patterns.

claim: Separation of pathways driving excitatory and inhibitory neurons would allow for independent activation (accelerator) or inactivation (brake) of movement.
source: This separation of pathways driving excitatory and inhibitory neurons would allow for independent activation (accelerator) or inactivation (brake) of movement (Callahan et al., 2019; Eklöf-Ljunggren et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation with citations to prior work (Callahan et al., 2019; Eklöf-Ljunggren et al., 2012).

claim: Synaptic inputs were measured during fictive locomotion induced by bright-field stimuli.
source: It is worth noting that we measured synaptic inputs during fictive locomotion induced by bright-field stimuli
evidence: This is a methodological statement about the experimental conditions.

claim: The possibility remains that sister vsx1 neurons do receive similar inputs under different behavioral paradigms, such as turns or escapes.

claim: It is unclear whether sister neurons are explicitly discouraged from sharing downstream targets or whether it is simply random.
source: Because we saw two examples of targets receiving input from both the V2a and V2b neuron of a clonal pair, it is unclear whether sister neurons are explicitly discouraged from sharing downstream targets or whether it is simply random.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the interpretation of the findings.

claim: The observed connectivity divergence might function to coordinate antagonistic components during locomotion.
source: In either case, the observed connectivity divergence might function to coordinate antagonistic components during locomotion.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: Spinal V1 interneurons target different populations of neurons along the rostral-caudal length of the spinal cord.
source: Spinal V1 interneurons target different populations of neurons along the rostral-caudal length of the spinal cord (Sengupta et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Sengupta et al., 2021).

claim: Even if non-clonally related V2a and V2b neurons generally form synaptic contacts onto the same populations, such as motor neurons, they may exhibit different connectivity patterns in the longitudinal axis, preventing clonally related pairs from sharing downstream targets.
